source_snapshot.items: LC.1_LC Tray Leak - Small Leak Detection
source_snapshot.procedure: A person triggers a small slow-dripping liquid leak in a tray using PG25.
source_snapshot.criteria: The tray detects the leak, turns off, and sends the correct BMC signals.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO/MANUAL; correctly requires a human physical leak but omits coolant quantity/location, interlocks, what turns off, signal IDs, timing, containment and recovery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/HIGH; retained Pending for qualified PG25 stimulus, hardware response map, BMC evidence and cleanup/recovery.

old_problem: The hazardous physical stimulus is described only as 'slow dripping'; the source does not identify leak point/rate/volume/duration, the sensor and affected actuator, what 'turn off' means, expected BMC identifiers/timing, or an authoritative decontamination/recovery procedure.
disposition_reason: Pending remains because the missing shutoff identity and coolant/recovery envelope are core hardware semantics and safety controls, not mere runtime IPs. ED-09 requires qualified human handling, while ED-15/16/20 prohibit guessing which valve, pump, tray rail or system power must turn off and what signal/timing constitutes PASS. A complete MANUAL ONLY draft is ready once the liquid-cooling owner supplies the approved physical procedure and recovery.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2093, same-row DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2094 / Wistron-HW-00470-V002 / 589798229c707371 was directly read from XLSX and manifest.
PG25 handling and physical dripping cannot be performed or substituted by an agent; qualified hardware personnel own stimulus, observation, containment and cleanup.
Small/slow is not a measurable safety envelope: an approved leak point, fixture, rate, maximum volume and duration are required before coolant approaches hardware.
The criterion 'turn off' must map to exact sensor, valve/pump/rail/system states and permitted transition sequence; a BMC alarm alone cannot prove physical shutoff.
Expected Redfish/SEL/event identifiers, severities and maximum detection/shutoff/reporting times must be signed before PASS can be judged.
Pre-test power/interlock state, PPE, absorbent containment, spill response, electrical isolation and stop conditions are mandatory.
Physical photos/video and timestamped BMC evidence must be preserved before cleanup; use only owner-approved drying, inspection, leak reset and return-to-service steps.
No leak, PG25 handling, valve/pump/power action, BMC query, cleanup, recovery or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: Qualified controlled PG25 tray small-leak response — PROCEDURE PENDING
test_case.purpose: Under an approved coolant-safety envelope, physically demonstrate that a small PG25 leak at the designated tray location is detected, drives the exact required local shutoff, reports the specified BMC signals within limits, and can be safely contained and restored.
required_package: Liquid-cooling owner-approved PG25 material, fixture, leak point, rate, maximum volume and duration
Qualified hardware operator, PPE, spill/electrical containment and emergency isolation
Tray/sensor/valve/pump/rail/system-power map and exact shutdown sequence
Expected Redfish/SEL signal IDs, severities and detection/shutoff/reporting limits
Approved cleanup, drying/exposure inspection, leak-reset and return-to-service procedure
test_case.test_command: NO REMOTE EXECUTION COMMAND. Do not introduce coolant until the physical and recovery contract is signed. Qualified personnel establish containment and record the mapped hardware/BMC baseline, then after point approval create one controlled PG25 drip at the approved point within the exact rate/volume/duration cap. Timestamp the stimulus, sensor detection, each required actuator/power transition and BMC events. Stop flow at the first limit or anomaly, preserve physical/log evidence, then perform only the approved containment, cleanup, inspection, reset and restoration. Never repeat after a failed response.
test_case.expected_result: Cannot be finalized until 'turn off' and signal/timing semantics are signed. The controlled leak must be detected by the designated sensor, the exact required hardware states must transition within limits, the specified BMC identifiers/severity must correlate, coolant must remain contained, and post-cleanup inspection/restoration must meet the approved oracle.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS while leak envelope, shutoff identity, signal matrix, limits and recovery are unresolved. After unlock, PASS requires one in-envelope physical stimulus, complete observed response/timing, correct BMC correlation, successful containment and authorized restored state. FAIL on missed/late detection, wrong or absent shutoff/signal, limit exceedance, coolant escape, unsafe exposure or recovery failure.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until qualified personnel, coolant envelope, interlocks, response map and recovery are approved.
Require immediate human point approval before the sole physical leak stimulus.
Protect energized electronics/personnel and verify containment/emergency isolation before fluid is released.
Stop immediately on uncontrolled flow, delayed/missing shutoff/alarm or exposure beyond the approved zone; no retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and signed manual procedure/JSA
Operator qualification, PG25 batch/spec, fixture, leak point/rate/volume/duration and pre-test photos
Mapped tray/sensor/valve/pump/power/BMC assets and physical/log baseline
Timestamped photo/video of one stimulus, detection and every required shutoff state
Complete protected Redfish/SEL event IDs, severity and correlation timeline
Contained-fluid accounting, cleanup/drying/exposure inspection, reset/restoration, no-retry audit and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On any containment breach, late/missing response, unexpected power action or coolant exposure, stop the source and invoke the approved emergency isolation/spill plan. Preserve evidence before cleanup; qualified personnel alone may dry, inspect, reset and release the system. Do not re-energize or repeat until owner clearance.

source_conflict.reason: The source is brief but not internally contradictory; the unresolved items are authoritative hardware/safety prerequisites.

blocked.reason: Static review and manual draft are complete; execution waits for a specific approved physical procedure and response/recovery contract.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Approved PG25 stimulus envelope, hardware shutoff identity/sequence, BMC signals/timings, safe power/interlocks, containment and recovery.
pending.execution_status: ENGINEERING DECISION RETAINED; PHYSICAL COOLANT TEST GATE CLOSED; NO LEAK, PG25 HANDLING, VALVE/PUMP/POWER ACTION, BMC QUERY, CLEANUP, RECOVERY OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: Liquid-cooling hardware/safety owner with BMC and platform owners
pending.unlock_condition: A signed liquid-cooling test procedure defines measurable stimulus, exact shutoff semantics, expected BMC events/timing, containment and complete cleanup/restoration; then re-review.

external_authorities.application: Keeps the physical action human-owned and forbids invented response criteria, unsafe automation, retry or recovery.

project_authority: Liquid-cooling/safety owner defines and supervises stimulus/containment/recovery; hardware owner defines shutoff; BMC owner defines signals; qualified operator performs actions and engineer owns verdict.
